summary: All 23 SRanger requirements are implemented in 9 Java files under sranger/ and traced in result_codegen.json. 9 points flagged: 2 invented defaults, 5 design choices, 1 ambiguous requirement, 1 scope question; nothing unimplemented.

issues.title: No-reading IR distance is 1000.0 m
issues.raw: SR-DM5 requires a 'large default value' when no reading is available but gives no number. Sensor returns NO_READING_DISTANCE = 1000.0 m (far beyond any IR range) until a valid reading arrives and after clearReading().
issues.fix_directive: Replace 1000.0 if the platform specifies a different no-reading value; it must stay above OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD.

issues.title: clockResetTime starts at 0.0
issues.raw: SR-Var1 defines clockResetTime only from the first entry into Turning. The field is initialised to 0.0; it is read only in Turning, after Moving -> Turning has reset it.
issues.fix_directive: None needed unless an initial value is specified.

issues.title: Move is one output event record with two real components
issues.raw: SR-DM4 gives one output event carrying two reals. Implemented as record Move(double lv, double av), not as a single component of a datatype or as two events (which SR-DM4 forbids). The profile's examples show events with at most one component.
issues.fix_directive: If the transformation cannot type a two-component event, wrap lv and av in a record type and give Move that single component.

issues.title: Moving -> Turning: obstacle event versus obstacleDetected guard
issues.raw: SR-Beh2 triggers the transition on the obstacle event alone; SR-GP1 says obstacleDetected is its guard. SR-DM3 says the event fires when the distance crosses below (strict) the threshold, SR-GP1 tests distance <= threshold. Implemented as trigger obstacle with guard obstacleDetected (<=), so a spurious obstacle event with no valid reading does not turn the robot (SR-DM5).
issues.fix_directive: Drop the guard if the event alone must trigger the turn.

issues.title: Initial Move(moveVel, 0) issued in the constructor
issues.raw: SR-FR1 issues Move(moveVel, 0) on entering Moving, and SR-Beh1 enters Moving at power-up, but no step() branch leads into the initial mode. The constructor issues the command once.
issues.fix_directive: None needed unless start-up must wait for the first event.

issues.title: Transition priority within Moving and Turning
issues.raw: The requirements give no priorities. endTask (a stop that applies in both modes) is the first branch of each. In Turning, the timed exit is above the tick self-loop, and the tick branch conjoins !turnDurationElapsed so the model's alternatives do not overlap. A tick arriving after turnDuration therefore returns the robot to Moving. Events with no transition in the current mode (obstacle in Turning, anything in Final) are ignored.
issues.fix_directive: Reorder if the shutdown must not take priority over the timed exit.

issues.title: obstacleThreshold 0.5 is rounded up to 1 in the model
issues.raw: OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD = 0.5 is the only fractional constant; the model's constants interface rounds it up to 1, so the model's obstacleDetected guard reads distance() <= 1. distance() is a sensor function in the model, so deadlock and divergence results do not depend on the value, but any obligation about the threshold's exact value would use 1. MOVE_VEL, TURN_VEL and TURN_DURATION are whole numbers and are not affected.
issues.fix_directive: None in the Java; the Java keeps the specified 0.5.

issues.title: Clock is a framework-advanced time source, held in field timer
issues.raw: The requirements need 'the current time' but do not name a source. Clock holds a monotonic time in seconds advanced by update(); now() reads it. The controller field is named timer because clock is a RoboChart reserved word. clockResetTime = timer.now() and timer.now() - clockResetTime >= TURN_DURATION follow the clock convention.

issues.title: Invalid readings mean no reading; Sensor and Actuator are classes
issues.raw: A negative or NaN measurement passed to Sensor.update() is treated as no reading (the large default), keeping distance() non-negative (SR-DM5). SR-ARCH2 calls the Sensor and Actuator 'interfaces'; they are concrete classes, following the profile's examples.

next_step: Run the pipeline. If a transformation phase rejects the Move event, start with the 'Move is one output event record' issue.
